assessment.nobel_worthiness: Defines a clear, discernible change in medicine: the physiology of proglucagon-derived peptides and GLP-1 as an incretin, leading to receptor-agonist therapies that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and show benefit in cardiovascular and renal outcomes. Both the basic mechanism and the clinical consequence are exceptionally strong.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and GLP-1 secretion in humans), Drucker (intestinotrophic and glucose-regulating actions, translation) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and early peptide work) form the most defensible trio from the credited names. Knudsen's industrial development of long-acting analogues is important but is drug development; the list also omits other early contributors such as Habener, which I cannot resolve from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, large randomized trials and wide clinical use; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit is contested among several groups and the longlist's names do not cover every early contributor.
Whether the committee prefers to reward the physiology or the drug-development component, and the long-term safety profile, remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a new intracellular signalling principle, communication from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with a defined mechanism (Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing) and broad relevance to secretory physiology, neurodegeneration, diabetes and cancer. A conceptually original and clean discovery in the mould of fundamental cell biology prizes.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the two decisive contributors by my knowledge: Mori identified the UPR elements and the pathway in yeast and mammals, Walter identified Ire1 and its unconventional splicing mechanism. A two-person prize is clean with no obvious omission among the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed and extended for over twenty years; the clinical translation is still developing but the basic discovery is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Some contributions by other labs (for example Sidrauski, Ron on PERK/eIF2alpha arm) are not in the credited names and could raise scope questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics is a methodological invention that changed how neural circuits are causally tested and spread across physiology; it combines microbial opsin discovery with the realization that genetically targeted opsins can control specified cells. Impact on neuroscience is enormous and ongoing.
assessment.attribution: Credit is complicated: Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann characterized channelrhodopsin; Boyden and Deisseroth demonstrated neuronal control; Miesenboeck contributed an earlier genetically targeted photostimulation concept. A three-person split of Nagel, Hegemann and Deisseroth balances the discovery of the tool and its neuronal implementation but necessarily leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and reproduced for over fifteen years; clinical use is emerging in vision restoration, so recognition is mature for the research tool.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit is the principal obstacle; the number of deserving names exceeds three.
The prize is for physiology or medicine; a tool's direct medical effect is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established that a gene could drive cancer by blocking cell death rather than by promoting proliferation, opening the field of apoptosis regulation and leading to BH3 mimetics such as venetoclax. A clear conceptual shift with a successful therapeutic consequence.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the cloning and characterization of the BCL-2 translocation and its family; Vaux showed the survival function of BCL-2 in cells and in cooperation with Myc. Strasser's later work on BCL-2 family members and in vivo roles is important, but the three-person set best fits the original finding. Others outside the list (Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto) may have competing claims, which I cannot assess from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, clinical validation with approved drugs, and a stable interpretation; timely.
uncertainties: Priority claims concerning the t(14;18) translocation and BCL-2 function involve other laboratories not on the longlist.
Whether the committee prefers the basic apoptosis control or the therapeutic component is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new treatment modality; the concept and the clinical proof are both highly original and impactful.
assessment.attribution: June and Sadelain are the clearest leaders of the CAR design and clinical translation (costimulatory domains, CD19 CARs, first trials). Rosenberg contributed adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell therapy, but earlier CAR concepts (Eshhar, not credited here) complicate the allocation; this is a fair configuration only if the committee accepts exclusion of those earlier works.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and long follow-up; still maturing for solid tumours and toxicity management, but the core discovery is established.
uncertainties: Priority and credit among Eshhar, Rosenberg, June and Sadelain are contested.
Long-term safety and the limited success in solid tumours remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of cGAS as the cytosolic DNA sensor producing cGAMP and STING as the adaptor defines a central innate-immune pathway with implications in infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer. A clear mechanistic discovery with wide reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING. This pair captures the pathway's two decisive discoveries from the credited names; Ishikawa, Sun and Wu contributed to important aspects but are not essential for a minimal configuration.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and mechanistically stable; therapeutic translation is not yet established clinically, so recognition might be slightly early.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit of STING agonists or antagonists is unproven.
Credit with other contributors to cyclic dinucleotide signalling is not captured by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the central regulator of cell growth and its nutrient-sensing network is a foundational concept in cell physiology with implications for cancer, ageing, diabetes and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and established its function; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and key components of nutrient sensing. Schreiber's work on FKBP12-rapamycin was important for the mechanism but is better treated as part of the chemical-biology origin; I leave him out to keep the discovery focused.
assessment.maturity: Extensively replicated and stable; therapeutic implications through rapalogs are established, though broader clinical promise is still developing.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Sabatini, Schreiber and others (e.g. Sabatini's professional conduct issues, which I cannot evaluate) is uncertain.
The prize may be argued to be better directed at a narrower component.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that a rationally designed inhibitor of the BCR-ABL kinase can produce durable remissions in chronic myeloid leukaemia, establishing the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy and converting a fatal disease into a manageable one.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (clinical translation and proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation therapy) can support a three-person configuration. Earlier discoveries of the Philadelphia chromosome and ABL fusion are recognized elsewhere or not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of outcome data and replicated results; recognition has been long awaited, with prior Lasker recognition.
uncertainties: The therapeutic nature of this candidate may favour the clinical side over a fundamental discovery.
Credit sharing with Janet Rowley, Nowell, Hungerford and Gleevec's other chemists is not captured.
